name: Warren Buffett
main_ideas: Buy wonderful companies at fair prices
Be fearful when others are greedy, greedy when others are fearful
Long-term holding beats frequent trading
Circle of competence — invest in what you understand
quote: Rule No. 1: Never lose money. Rule No. 2: Never forget Rule No. 1.
relevance: The most successful investor of all time. His value investing philosophy and folksy wisdom have guided generations of investors toward long-term thinking.

name: Charlie Munger
main_ideas: Build a latticework of mental models from multiple disciplines
Invert, always invert — think about what to avoid
Patience and discipline are the investor's greatest tools
Avoid stupidity rather than seeking brilliance
quote: It is remarkable how much long-term advantage people like us have gotten by trying to be consistently not stupid, instead of trying to be very intelligent.
relevance: Buffett's indispensable partner and the architect of multidisciplinary thinking in investing. His mental models framework influenced decision-making far beyond finance.

name: Ray Dalio
main_ideas: Radical transparency and idea meritocracy lead to better decisions
Understand the macroeconomic machine — debt cycles drive everything
Diversify across uncorrelated assets for an all-weather portfolio
Pain plus reflection equals progress
key_works: Principles for Dealing with the Changing World Order
quote: He who lives by the crystal ball will eat shattered glass.
relevance: Founder of the world's largest hedge fund, Bridgewater Associates. His principles-based approach and macroeconomic frameworks have reshaped institutional investing.

name: Benjamin Graham
main_ideas: Margin of safety — always buy below intrinsic value
Mr. Market is emotional; exploit his mood swings rationally
Distinguish between investment and speculation
Thorough analysis of financial statements is essential
quote: In the short run, the market is a voting machine but in the long run, it is a weighing machine.
relevance: The father of value investing and security analysis. His frameworks for evaluating stocks remain the bedrock of fundamental analysis nearly a century later.

name: Peter Lynch
main_ideas: Invest in what you know — everyday observations reveal great companies
Do your homework before investing, not after
Tenbaggers are found by patient, informed investors
Know the story behind every stock you own
quote: Know what you own, and know why you own it.
relevance: Managed the Magellan Fund to a 29% average annual return over 13 years. His accessible approach empowered individual investors to compete with professionals.

name: Jack Bogle
main_ideas: Low-cost index funds outperform most active managers over time
Costs matter — every dollar in fees is a dollar less in returns
Stay the course through market turbulence
Simplicity beats complexity in investing
key_works: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing
Enough: True Measures of Money, Business, and Life
quote: Don't look for the needle in the haystack. Just buy the haystack!
relevance: Founder of Vanguard and creator of the first index fund for individual investors. He single-handedly saved investors trillions of dollars in unnecessary fees.

name: Robert Kiyosaki
main_ideas: Assets put money in your pocket; liabilities take it out
Financial literacy is more important than a high income
The rich don't work for money — they make money work for them
Pay yourself first, even when it feels uncomfortable
quote: The single most powerful asset we all have is our mind. If it is trained well, it can create enormous wealth.
relevance: Introduced millions of people worldwide to financial literacy through simple, compelling stories. His asset vs. liability framework changed how everyday people think about money.

name: George Soros
main_ideas: Markets are driven by reflexivity — perceptions alter fundamentals, and fundamentals alter perceptions
Find the prevailing bias and bet heavily when it becomes unsustainable
Survival comes first; profit comes second
It's not whether you're right or wrong that matters, but how much you make when right
key_works: The New Paradigm for Financial Markets
quote: It's not whether you're right or wrong that's important, but how much money you make when you're right and how much you lose when you're wrong.
relevance: Known as the man who broke the Bank of England. His theory of reflexivity challenged efficient market assumptions and revealed how perception shapes financial reality.

name: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
main_ideas: Black swans — rare, unpredictable events dominate history and markets
Antifragility — position yourself to gain from disorder, not just survive it
Skin in the game — never trust advice from those with nothing to lose
Barbell strategy — combine extreme safety with small, high-upside bets
quote: Wind extinguishes a candle and energizes fire. Likewise with randomness, uncertainty, chaos: you want to use them, not hide from them.
relevance: Transformed how the world thinks about risk, uncertainty, and resilience. His concept of antifragility extends far beyond finance into philosophy and daily life.

name: Howard Marks
main_ideas: Second-level thinking — go beyond the obvious consensus
Understanding market cycles is the key to avoiding catastrophic losses
Risk means more things can happen than will happen
The most profitable investments are uncomfortable to make
quote: You can't predict. You can prepare.
relevance: Co-founder of Oaktree Capital and master of distressed debt investing. His memos on market cycles and risk are considered essential reading on Wall Street.

name: Carl Icahn
main_ideas: Undervalued companies with poor management are prime targets
Shareholder activism can unlock hidden value
Challenge entrenched boards to drive corporate accountability
Buy undervalued assets and push for structural change
key_works: SEC Filings and Public Letters to Boards
quote: In life and business, there are two cardinal sins. The first is to act precipitously without thought, and the second is to not act at all.
relevance: The original corporate raider turned shareholder advocate. His aggressive activist style forced corporate America to take shareholder value seriously.

name: Paul Tudor Jones
main_ideas: Defense is more important than offense — control losses first
Trend following and technical analysis reveal market psychology
The most important rule of trading is to play great defense
Never average losers — cut losses quickly and let winners run
quote: The secret to being successful from a trading perspective is to have an indefatigable and an undying and unquenchable thirst for information and knowledge.
relevance: Predicted and profited from the 1987 Black Monday crash. His macro trading approach and emphasis on risk management set the standard for hedge fund traders.

name: Jesse Livermore
main_ideas: The market is never wrong; opinions are
Let profits run and cut losses short
Timing and patience are everything in speculation
Study the behavior of the market, not tips or rumors
key_works: Jesse Livermore's Methods of Trading in Stocks
quote: There is nothing new in Wall Street. There can't be because speculation is as old as the hills.
relevance: The greatest speculator of the early twentieth century, making and losing multiple fortunes. His trading wisdom, captured in Reminiscences of a Stock Operator, remains a must-read classic.

name: André Kostolany
main_ideas: Buy shares, take sleeping pills, and stop watching the market
The stock market is like a man walking his dog — the dog runs ahead and behind, but both end up at the same destination
Think independently and resist the herd mentality
Patience is the supreme virtue of the investor
quote: Buy when the cannons are thundering, sell when the violins are playing.
relevance: Europe's most beloved stock market philosopher and storyteller. His witty aphorisms and contrarian wisdom made investing accessible to millions of German-speaking investors.

name: John Templeton
main_ideas: Maximum pessimism is the best time to buy; maximum optimism is the best time to sell
Diversify globally — opportunity exists everywhere on the planet
Bargain hunting across borders yields the best returns
Humility and gratitude are essential for long-term success
quote: The four most dangerous words in investing are: 'This time it's different.'
relevance: Pioneer of global investing who bought depressed stocks across the world when others feared to look abroad. His contrarian discipline and spiritual approach to wealth remain deeply influential.

name: Philip Fisher
main_ideas: Scuttlebutt — talk to customers, competitors, and suppliers to evaluate a company
Buy outstanding companies and hold them for decades
Quality of management is the most critical factor in investing
A few great investments over a lifetime outperform many mediocre ones
key_works: Paths to Wealth Through Common Stocks
quote: The stock market is filled with individuals who know the price of everything, but the value of nothing.
relevance: The father of growth investing whose scuttlebutt research method influenced Warren Buffett and generations of investors. His emphasis on qualitative analysis complemented Graham's quantitative approach.

name: Burton Malkiel
main_ideas: A blindfolded monkey throwing darts can match most professional stock pickers
Markets are largely efficient — prices already reflect available information
Broad index funds are the smartest choice for most investors
Past performance does not predict future results
key_works: A Random Walk Down Wall Street
From Wall Street to the Great Wall
quote: A blindfolded monkey throwing darts at a newspaper's financial pages could select a portfolio that would do just as well as one carefully selected by experts.
relevance: His Random Walk Down Wall Street is the most influential book arguing for passive investing. His academic work provided the intellectual foundation for the index fund revolution.

name: William O'Neil
main_ideas: CAN SLIM — a systematic framework combining fundamentals and technicals
Buy stocks breaking out to new highs with strong earnings and volume
Cut every loss at 7-8% without exception
Study historical chart patterns of the greatest winning stocks
key_works: How to Make Money in Stocks
quote: The whole secret to winning and losing in the stock market is to lose the least amount possible when you're not right.
relevance: Created the CAN SLIM method and founded Investor's Business Daily. His systematic, rules-based approach bridged fundamental and technical analysis for growth stock investors.

name: Cathie Wood
main_ideas: Invest in disruptive innovation before the market recognizes its potential
Convergence of technologies — AI, robotics, genomics, blockchain — creates exponential growth
Traditional valuation models fail for truly transformative companies
A five-year time horizon captures what others miss
key_works: In the Know with Cathie Wood (podcast)
quote: Innovation solves problems. The bigger the problem, the bigger the opportunity.
relevance: Founder of ARK Invest and a bold voice for disruptive innovation investing. Her conviction-driven, research-heavy approach polarizes but has inspired a new generation of forward-looking investors.

name: Michael Burry
main_ideas: Independent, deep research uncovers what the herd ignores
Contrarian bets require the courage to be early and endure pain
Read the footnotes — hidden risks live in the details
Concentrated positions in high-conviction ideas yield outsized returns
quote: I was wrong about everything early. I was just less wrong than everybody else.
relevance: Foresaw and profited from the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis, as depicted in The Big Short. His obsessive, detail-oriented research style epitomizes independent thinking in investing.
